questions.stem: This PA chest radiograph shows hyperlucent, hyperinflated lungs with flattened hemidiaphragms and a narrow vertical cardiac silhouette. These findings are most typical of which condition?

explanation.summary: In emphysema, air trapping expands lung volumes, flattening the diaphragms, increasing lung lucency, widening the retrosternal space, and narrowing the heart shadow. These are the classic radiographic signs of COPD hyperinflation.
explanation.whyCorrect: In emphysema, air trapping expands lung volumes, flattening the diaphragms, increasing lung lucency, widening the retrosternal space, and narrowing the heart shadow. These are the classic radiographic signs of COPD hyperinflation.

questions.stem: On this lateral chest radiograph (trachea, lungs, and heart labeled), which finding is specifically assessed as a sign of hyperinflation in COPD?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Deviation of the trachea to one side

explanation.summary: The lateral view demonstrates hyperinflation as an increased lucent retrosternal air space and flattening of the diaphragm. This complements the flattened diaphragms and hyperlucency seen on the frontal film.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lateral view demonstrates hyperinflation as an increased lucent retrosternal air space and flattening of the diaphragm. This complements the flattened diaphragms and hyperlucency seen on the frontal film.

questions.stem: This classic clinical illustration shows an elderly man with marked muscle wasting and a barrel-shaped chest sitting forward. Which COPD phenotype is being depicted?

explanation.summary: The cachectic, barrel-chested patient who leans forward and uses accessory muscles represents the emphysema-predominant 'pink puffer,' who maintains near-normal oxygenation through increased work of breathing rather than becoming cyanotic and edematous.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cachectic, barrel-chested patient who leans forward and uses accessory muscles represents the emphysema-predominant 'pink puffer,' who maintains near-normal oxygenation through increased work of breathing rather than becoming cyanotic and edematous.
